topic: How does defocused feed array placement optimize coverage versus scan loss in DBF architectures?
consensus_response: Defocused feed array placement optimizes coverage versus scan loss by introducing a gradual tapering of the array factor, mitigating interference between adjacent elements. This reduces spillover losses (4.95 dB at 2 dB scan) and minimizes the impact of failed components, resulting in improved coverage and reduced scan loss. The trade-off is a slightly reduced gain (1.35 dB at 2 dB scan), affecting the overall capacity and performance of the system. Defocused reflectors demonstrate robustness under failure conditions, with reduced gain loss when individual or multiple feed elements drop out.
reference_context: Defocused feed array placement reduces spillover losses by 4.95 dB at 2 dB scan, while introducing taper losses of 1.35 dB. The defocused reflector concept is robust against feed failures, suffering less from gain loss compared to conventional reflectors.
